tagline: Up from the Toe River to the Roan's balds and rhododendron.
intro: From Micaville the byway takes NC 80 north beside the Toe River, past Kona and over to Bakersville, the Mitchell County seat in the valley of Cane Creek. There NC 261 starts uphill. It climbs into the Pisgah National Forest, over Pumpkin Patch Gap and along Little Rock Creek, then through a run of hairpins to Carvers Gap at about 5,500 feet, where the Appalachian Trail crosses on the state line.
That last climb was a gravel and dirt road until the state paved it between 1949 and 1953. Christmas tree farms are scattered through the hills on the way up.
season: Mid to late June, when the Catawba rhododendron gardens on Roan Mountain bloom.

moments.title: Kona
moments.text: A crossroads on NC 80 near where the North and South Toe rivers meet, named for the chemistry of feldspar: K for potassium, O for oxygen, Na for sodium.

moments.title: Bakersville
moments.text: The county seat rode a mica boom in the 1870s and is home to the North Carolina Rhododendron Festival, which drew Richard Nixon in 1958.

moments.title: Roan Mountain
moments.text: From the gap the Appalachian Trail heads east over Grassy Ridge, the longest stretch of grassy bald in the Appalachians, and the byway's last spur runs west to the rhododendron gardens.

practical: The spur road from Carvers Gap to the rhododendron gardens is closed in winter, and the gardens charge a small parking fee.
